comments.author: Tempest1981
comments.story: An Inconvenient Truth about Smart Cities
comments.why: Details of EPCOT's circular city, monorails and people movers
comments.text: The full EPCOT plans are interesting. A circular city layout, with layers. Density in the center. People taking monorails to work, and WEDway people movers locally. Designed for biking and walking. Cars only used on weekends. Details about 10 min into this video: [VIDEO]

comments.author: blotter_paper
comments.story: Should Disney World Have the Right to Build a Nuclear Power Plant?
comments.why: Disney's original plan for the land and EPCOT city
comments.text: And those legal machinations were arranged by a lawyer who used to be a CIA recruiter. I'll add this video of Walt Disney's original plan for the land, in which Disney World is overshadowed by the (u/dys)topian city he called EPCOT (later mangled into the showroom we know today by his brother and investors who were scared of costs and didn't see reliable earning potential in running a city) with a timestamp to when the fun starts: [VIDEO] This is the stuff that inspired BioShock and similar settings (I believe I read an interview years ago where one of the designers mentioned it as an influence, but I wouldn't know where to find a link).

comments.author: padobson
comments.story: When Disney Got Adult and Trippy
comments.text: "Industry pundits predicted that no one would sit still for a cartoon feature. Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs proved otherwise and blazed the trail for the industry." Nobody knew how to make serious money on short animations, animated features, or theme parks before Walt Disney. He did it all though. He also wanted to try out the utopia thing[1], and it's maybe the 20th century's greatest missed opportunity. If you haven't read Walt Disney's World[2], it's my favorite biography on the great man.
